statement.excerpt: To be sure I don’t expect LLMs to disappear anytime soon but the valuations and market caps we are currently seeing may eventually be seen as ludicrous.

from_speaker: I don’t expect LLMs to disappear
our_interpretation: Assess the listed proposition about LLM persistence, not the separate possibility that valuations may eventually look ludicrous.
The plain reading is that LLMs will remain practically available and used in the near term.
'I don’t expect' expresses a directional forecast; it is not a conditional antecedent.
'Anytime soon' gives no calendar deadline. No arbitrary number of months is supplied.
Retirement of particular models or products does not amount to disappearance of LLMs as a technology.
criteria.support_condition: LLMs remain practically available and used through a defensible endpoint for the speaker's near-term horizon; no such endpoint is specified here.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive near-term cessation of practical LLM availability and use establishes that LLMs have disappeared in the ordinary sense.
